target:
Wall thickness for the absorber comes to 26 mm after the corrosion allowance is added. The allowance is metal given up to corrosion over the vessel life, and the pressure case is checked on the corroded thickness; a shell sized on the thickness as fabricated would meet the pressure requirement on delivery and lose it as corrosion proceeds. The stated thickness is the figure the fabrication drawing carries, and the figure the inspection plan measures against.

Gasket selection for the flange joints turns on temperature limit alone. Two materials are under consideration, and each seals the joint at the design pressure; the difference between them is the temperature each withstands at the joint face, and the higher-rated material is preferred. A gasket that softens at operating temperature loses bolt load as the joint heats, and the joint then weeps at the flange face; a rating above the operating temperature keeps the bolt load the joint was assembled with.
